scope: Bounded current scholarly-method/source census; not complete original SUNNY research coverage.
exposure: Molin primary publication connector text already inspected

questions.question: Who has proposed this or something structurally equivalent before?
questions.answer: Molin2020 supplies comparative pausal/contextual reconstructions; DeCaen/Dresher2020 discuss prosodic domains and pausal forms. Relational functional-dependency theory supplies the mathematical consistency criterion.
questions.gap: Original source editions and whole scholarly literature remain incompletely covered.

questions.question: What fields study this problem?
questions.answer: Historical Semitic phonology, biblical reading traditions, prosody/cantillation, manuscript transmission and relational/functional mathematics.
questions.gap: The fields do not by themselves establish a musical or geometric adapter.

questions.question: What terminology do those fields use for it?
questions.answer: Pausal/contextual form; qames/ṣere; vocalic shewa; matres lectionis; stress; intonational/phonological phrase; functional dependency; information-losing projection.
questions.gap: Similar terms across traditions do not establish identical operations.

questions.question: What are the closest established theories, models, equations, or frameworks?
questions.answer: Context-conditioned phonological relations and prosodic-domain models; exact finite relation and functional-dependency tests.
questions.gap: The intended complete SUNNY geometry and original-sound map are not derived by these methods.

questions.question: What reviews, surveys, bibliographies, encyclopedias, dissertations, or meta-analyses map the space?
questions.answer: The acquired2020 primary edited volume and its source bibliographies provide a bounded entry point; inherited14-question baseline retained.
questions.gap: No exhaustive cross-tradition survey has been completed.

questions.question: What are the canonical papers, books, and authors?
questions.answer: Inspected: Molin; DeCaen/Dresher; BerkeleyCS186 mathematical definitions. Shaked1995 and Naveh/Shaked1985 are cited-edition targets, not yet collated originals.
questions.gap: Field-wide canonical status is not inferred from these references.

questions.question: What are the competing explanations?
questions.answer: Context/lexeme/historical-vowel distinctions; tradition/witness differences; prosodic-domain versus accent-label rules; orthographic versus phonetic interpretation.
questions.gap: No single additional argument or historical explanation selected by source repetition or model preference.

questions.question: What has been falsified, criticized, or abandoned?
questions.answer: Within the admitted comparative pairs, a deterministic map from surface[a]andpausealone has incompatible outputs. Source-proposed same-accent counterexamples oppose an accent-only pause decoder.
questions.gap: These conditional counterexamples do not falsify a richer original-symbol system or establish ancient sounds.

questions.question: What are the unresolved questions?
questions.answer: Original ink, cited edition locators, specimen dating, transcription-to-phone licensing, source-specific grammar and applicability to new words remain unresolved.
questions.gap: A unique global alignment and universal phonological rule remain open.

questions.question: What primary sources or datasets are important to the field?
questions.answer: Exa versioned primary-volume rendering, exactMolinspans, independent source-review ledgers, actual local Jev62 receipt.
questions.gap: Connector text is not byte-identical original PDF or independently observed inscription.

questions.question: What earlier historical traditions have scholars already connected to it?
questions.answer: Molin compares bowl quotations with later Babylonian manuscript reconstructions and Tiberian written comparanda; DeCaen/Dresher analyze Tiberian prosody.
questions.gap: Do not silently transfer Tiberian accent/domain rules into unpointed Babylonian bowls.

questions.question: Has terminology changed over time in ways that hide older versions?
questions.answer: Received spelling, reconstructed pronunciation, notation and grammar have different histories; pausal and contextual are source-defined roles, not measured silence.
questions.gap: Historical terminology and original phonological categories need source-specific recovery.

questions.question: Have adjacent disciplines rediscovered the same structure under another name?
questions.answer: Same-input/different-output conflicts are also studied as failures of functional dependency and as failure of an operation to descend through a quotient.
questions.gap: This structural reuse is not a new general theorem or a cross-domain historical identity.

questions.question: What obvious prior-art searches have produced nothing?
questions.answer: No negative search establishes absence of prior art. Source acquisition and searches are recorded separately in the shaked/prosody directories.
questions.gap: The complete scholarly and controlled heterodox census remains unfinished.

heterodoxPhase.boundary: No completed First&3/4 Order census is claimed.
